$comment: Reproducibility pins: (published npm version) -> (commit whose build produces its exact dist bytes).
This is the evidence base for scripts/check-publish-drift.mjs. That detector's whole authority is
the claim 'this repo's dist output is byte-reproducible', because npm exposes no gitHead for these
packages. A claim the gate never re-tests is a phantom mechanism, so publish-drift.yml rebuilds a
pinned commit on every run and asserts --expect-in-sync before any drift verdict is trusted.
Add a new pin each time a version is published, in the release PR.

pins.note: release(sdk): 1.2.0 to npm (#3) — verified 2026-08-26: rebuild matches both published tarballs byte-for-byte

release-candidate 1.3.0 to npm — PENDING verification. Pin references the exact release-candidate SHA whose build produces the inspected 1.3.0 candidate dist (the version-bump commit 79d2101 plus the remediation commit that corrected the frihet login URL hint in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts, which materially changed the CLI dist bytes; the pre-remediation version-bump commit no longer produces the final 1.3.0 dist). Registry verification cannot run until 1.3.0 is actually published. After the release PR is squash-merged, the canonical main SHA may replace this reference only after a byte-comparison proves the squash-commit dist/** is identical to this candidate's dist/**; the note will then be updated to the verified form (matching the 1.2.0 pin's wording).
